title: Inside the Box
summary: Discover the CPU, memory, and storage.
objectives: Identify the CPU as the brain
Differentiate between short-term memory (RAM) and long-term storage

steps.boltSpeech: What's happening inside the computer case?

content.text: Inside the computer case (or inside the laptop body), there are important chips and drives working together.

points.text: CPU (Central Processing Unit): The brain. It does all the thinking and calculating.
RAM (Memory): Short-term memory. It holds what the computer is working on right NOW.
Storage (Hard Drive/SSD): Long-term memory. It saves your files even when the power is off.

questions.prompt: Which part is known as the 'brain' of the computer?
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) processes instructions, acting like a brain.

questions.prompt: If you want to save a picture forever, where does the computer put it?
questions.explanation: Storage keeps your files safe even when the computer is turned off. RAM is cleared when the power goes out.

steps.boltSpeech: Match the part to its human body equivalent!
steps.instructions: Sort the computer parts into Brain, Desk (Working space), or Filing Cabinet (Storage).
